label: Adam Smith
description: The 'internal witness' in Theory of Moral Sentiments.

label: Albert Einstein
description: General relativity; a determinist invoked on both sides.

label: Antony Flew
description: Prominent atheist turned deist over DNA evidence.

label: Aristotle
description: Defined nothing as 'what rocks dream about'.

label: Arno Penzias
description: Co-discovered the radiation echo; quoted on a balanced, supernatural-seeming universe.

label: Arthur Eddington
description: Called the cosmic beginning 'frankly supernatural'.

label: Blaise Pascal
description: Addressed those 'so made that they cannot believe'.

label: C. S. Lewis
description: Attributed conscience to the divine; Hitchens says without improving on Smith.

label: Chandra Wickramasinghe
description: Called primordial-soup belief 'an article of faith'.

label: Charles Darwin
description: Natural selection; Hitchens's 'greater emancipator'.

label: Daniel Dennett
description: Materialist who treats consciousness as an illusion.

label: David Hume
description: On miracles and the is-ought problem.

label: Edwin Hubble
description: Discovered cosmic expansion (1929).

label: Francis Collins
description: Supervisor of the Human Genome Project; Hitchens's 'occasional debating enemy', invoked on the age of Homo sapiens.

label: Francis Crick
description: Co-discoverer of DNA; floated panspermia.

label: Fred Hoyle
description: Coined 'Big Bang'; spoke of a superintellect monkeying with physics.

label: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Brothers Karamazov; his character Smerdyakov voices the 'everything is permitted' line.

label: George Smoot
description: Led the COBE result; quoted comparing it to looking at God.

label: Georges Lemaitre
description: Catholic physicist who first proposed the Big Bang.

label: H. L. Mencken
description: Listed thousands of dead gods in Hitchens's anthology.

label: Lawrence Krauss
description: On the increasing red-shift rate.

label: Lucretius
description: Atomic theory predating the morality debate; cited with Democritus and Epicurus.

label: Omar Khayyam
description: Persian poet whose quatrain Hitchens borrows to ask Turek 'what is your authority for saying you know something I don't?'.

label: Richard Dawkins
description: Hostile witness on DNA's information content.

label: Robert Jastrow
description: Agnostic astronomer; Turek's hostile witness for an abrupt creation.

label: Robert Wilson
description: Co-discovered the cosmic afterglow at Bell Labs.

label: Socrates
description: His inner daemon as a model of conscience.

label: Stephen Hawking
description: Invoked by both; Hitchens warns against drafting him as a deist.

label: Stephen Jay Gould
description: Panda's thumb (poor design) and non-overlapping magisteria.

label: Steven Weinberg
description: Atheist physicist on the delicate balance required for life.

label: Thomas Aquinas
description: Source of the ontological move Hitchens parodies.

label: Thomas Jefferson
description: Author of Virginia's statute on religious freedom; a deist.

label: William Gladstone
description: Scholar of Latin and Greek; cited as having shown Greek moral precepts as 'prefigurations of Christianity'.

label: William Paley
description: The watchmaker analogy: design implies a designer.

label: William Provine
description: Materialist Darwinist who denies free will.
